title: Developer-First API SDK with Type Safety & Auto-Generation
problem: Integrating REST APIs without strongly-typed client libraries forces engineering teams to write repetitive HTTP boilerplate, maintain fragile interface declarations, and handle network failures in an ad-hoc manner. When backend API schemas evolve, unsynchronized frontend and backend codebases fail silently at runtime rather than at compile time. This project builds a code-generation pipeline and runtime SDK engine that parses OpenAPI 3.0 specifications into idiomatic TypeScript client packages, featuring request authentication, exponential retry logic with jitter, local sandbox mocking, and dual CommonJS and ECMAScript module distribution bundles.
use_cases: Enterprise developer platforms publishing typed client packages for public REST APIs
Internal microservice communication libraries ensuring synchronized API contract types
Offline-capable developer testing sandboxes using schema-compliant mock responses
hard_parts: Resolving recursive schema references and circular dependencies in OpenAPI documents without stack overflow errors
Translating complex schema compositions into idiomatic TypeScript discriminated unions without falling back to any types
Ensuring dual CommonJS and ECMAScript module compatibility with clean declaration maps across different bundlers
Implementing exponential backoff with full jitter to avoid thundering herd retry storms against rate-limited backends
screener_signals: Clean CLI tool parsing OpenAPI specifications and emitting modular TypeScript source files
Zero compile-time errors under tsc strict mode with zero occurrences of the any type keyword
Vitest test suite validating automated retries, mock interceptors, and dual-module resolution

architecture.data_flow: The CLI parses OpenAPI specifications into an intermediate model; the code generator emits TypeScript interfaces and client classes; developers initialize the SDK client; runtime interceptors attach authorization headers and telemetry; native fetch executes HTTP requests; if a transient error occurs, exponential backoff retries the request; responses deserialize into validated typed objects.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Strict compile-time type verification via tsc --noEmit; runtime response status checks that throw structured API exceptions.

worksheet.q1: The student builds a TypeScript code generator that transforms OpenAPI specs into typed client packages featuring retry interceptors, mock sandboxing, and dual CJS/ESM bundling.
worksheet.q2: Core path: AST normalizer, TypeScript code generator, resilient runtime client, mock sandbox, and tsup packaging (29h). Extended path: automated npm publish workflow and SSE streaming client (+12h).
worksheet.q3: Components: Parser (5h), Generator (4h), Runtime Client (4h), Mock Sandbox (4h), Packaging (4h), Docs & Buffer (4h). Total 25h x 1.15 = 29h.
worksheet.q4: Project types: CLI/tools/libraries, API/backend. Metrics: Code Generation Latency, Type System Strictness, Transient Fault Retry Recovery. Rejected: high-concurrency gateway throughput (it's a client SDK generator, not a proxy server).
worksheet.q5: Hard parts: circular $ref dereferencing, discriminated union synthesis, dual CJS/ESM module compatibility, and exponential jitter retry calibration.
worksheet.q6: Starter input: 3 OpenAPI specification files (5 to 30 endpoints) containing recursive references, inheritance schemas, and rate limit definitions. No personal data.
worksheet.q7: Hardware: Linux/macOS/Windows, 8GB RAM, CPU only, $0 cost, zero cloud accounts. Fallback: standard tsc compiler mode without tsup.
worksheet.q8: Riskiest component: Circular schema dereferencing. Fallback: lazy type reference indirection.
worksheet.q9: Potential faking: pre-generated static TypeScript files. Anti-fake check 5 accepts dynamic OpenAPI spec at runtime and compiles and executes custom typed methods on the fly.
worksheet.q10: Safety/ethics: Not required for client SDK code generation.
